newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand bond yield curve flatten at close.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand bond yield curve flatten at close.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.95 PCT (PREV 7.95) US 5-YR 6.12 (PREV 6.21)
* NZ debt markets open stronger on back of U.S. Treasuries
* Curve flattens as long-end strengthens
* Direction next week will be set by Treasuries
The New Zealand bond curve flattened on Friday with 10-year bonds ending 10 points lower while the shorter bonds only fell three points.
Dealers said trading was choppy with bouts of aggressive trading.
One dealer suggested it was traders buying back short-position in the long bonds. He said there was some very aggressive selling in the 7/98 and 2/00 bonds.
The flattening trend is seen continuing and may even see the curve inverse.
The market was generally lead down by the rally in the U.S. Treasuries market overnight.
The 90-day bank bills were subdued in afternoon trade, with the yield ending little changed from Friday.
There was little notice taking of the government announcement on the division of the Finance Minister and Treasurer roles.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger said the Treasurer would have responsibility for the budget, the Reserve Bank and the Policy Target Agreement agreed with the bank.
There was slightly more interest and encouragement taken of reports that Treasurer Winston Peters would act to check spending.
The market similarly ignored an improved November trade deficit of $92 million.
-- Simon Louisson 64 4 4714 276
